statement: Congestion pricing in Manhattan's Central Business District (from 5 January 2025) raised taxi and for-hire vehicle speeds and reduced TLC trip counts in the CBD relative to the rest of New York City.

graph_evidence.note: The System graph holds no findings on road pricing, congestion charging or cordon tolls (variable searches: congestion pricing, road pricing, congestion charging, low emission zone, cordon, toll). This claim rests on the literature below; the gap is itself a research_needed item.

relevant_hits: Reduction in the incidence of casualties after a road traffic crash (from 1996-2001 to 2003-2008)
average traffic flow reduction (%) during COVID19 lockdown period

literature.citation: Eliasson J (2009). A cost-benefit analysis of the Stockholm congestion charging system. Transp Res A 43:468-480.
literature.finding: Traffic across the cordon fell about 20% and stayed lower.

literature.citation: Transport for London (2007). Central London Congestion Charging: Impacts monitoring, fifth annual report.
literature.finding: Traffic entering the zone fell about 18-21%; congestion (delay) fell about 30% at first and returned toward baseline by 2006.

literature.citation: Cook C, Kreidieh A, Vasserman S, Allcott H, Arora N, van Sambeek F, Tomkins A, Turkel E (2025). Short-run traffic effects of New York's congestion pricing. NBER working paper.
literature.finding: Reported faster travel in the CBD in early 2025 (cited from memory of the working paper; not verified here).

literature.citation: NYC DOHMH (14 August 2026). Congestion pricing air quality report (Environment and Health Data Portal).
literature.finding: States that traffic entering the zone fell about 10% in 2025 (secondary report, 6sqft, 17 Aug 2026).

prediction.magnitude: Difference-in-differences of log monthly taxi/FHV speed, CBD minus rest of city, 2025 vs 2024: +5% to +15%. Difference-in-differences of log monthly TLC trips (pickups plus drop-offs) in CBD taxi zones minus non-CBD zones, 2025 vs 2024: -3% to -12%.
prediction.support_if: Speed DiD > 0 with a 95% interval above 0, and the trip-count DiD below 0.
prediction.refute_if: Speed DiD <= 0 with an interval that excludes +3%, or CBD trips rise relative to outside.

plan: Data: MTA 'CBD Taxi and For-Hire Vehicle Speeds: Beginning October 2019' (data.ny.gov 6p29-6xqn), zones CBD vs rest of city (and adjacent area as a second comparison); TLC 'Pickups and Drop-offs by Taxi Zone and Industry' (data.cityofnewyork.us c5iv-bn4s) with the CBD zone list from MTA yfdc-w5jh; MTA 'Vehicle Miles Traveled in the CBD' (jbxx-kxff) as a descriptive check; MTA CRZ entries (t6yz-b64h) descriptive only because it starts in 2025. Unit: month. Model: OLS of log value on area, calendar month, year and area x post (post = Jan 2025 on), pre-period Jan 2023 - Dec 2024, post Jan - latest 2025/2026 month; HAC (Newey-West, 3 lags) standard errors. Pre-trend check: the same model with a placebo post = Jan 2024 on 2023-2024 only. Figure: monthly CBD and comparison series with the start date marked.
alternatives: Post-pandemic return-to-office trend that differs between the CBD and outer boroughs
Seasonal and weather shocks (absorbed in part by calendar-month terms; common shocks by the comparison)
Displacement: traffic avoiding the zone slows the comparison area, which inflates the DiD
Change in TLC fleet composition or app-company pricing unrelated to the toll (the HVFHV $1.50 and taxi $0.75 per-trip CBD surcharges are part of the policy itself)
registrant: mobility agent (Claude Opus 5.5), for J. Vernon
